_note: Sensors are mostly featureless boxes from the outside, so most prompts ask for a cutaway at the sensing element and name what makes that element different (a MEMS mirror instead of a spinning drum, patch antennas instead of a lens, a fiber coil instead of a chip). The depth cameras are separated by what they emit rather than by their housings. Anchor is 1, the spinning LiDAR, because it is the most recognizable shape on the sheet. Do not name copper anywhere: the house palette is steel-blue accents only, and naming the material makes the model add a warm accent that breaks the set.
_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, written after the per-entry attempt above was abandoned. These are exterior views of whole objects and never cutaways. The failure last time was that most sensors are a featureless box, so the prompts opened the box at the sensing element and the internals came back wrong. Here each class is identified by its aperture, which is visible from outside: a spinning drum with a window band, a flat board tiled with antenna patches, a protruding lens barrel, a sealed block with no opening at all, a slotted code disc, and a limp printed sheet. Each renders at about 74px, so every prompt asks for one centered object with a bold silhouette and no fine detail.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including wire, windings, coils, magnets and terminals, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model.

prompts.1: A mechanical spinning LiDAR: a squat cylindrical unit with a rotating upper drum and a continuous horizontal window band around it, cut away on one side to show a vertical stack of paired laser emitters and detectors aimed out through the window, sitting on a motor and slip ring in the base. Connector at the bottom.
prompts.2: A solid-state LiDAR: a compact rectangular box with a flat front window, cut away to show a small square MEMS mirror suspended on torsion flexures tilting a laser beam into a fan across the window. Nothing rotates, and there is no drum. The tiny mirror is the focus.
prompts.3: An FMCW LiDAR built on silicon photonics, deliberately not a spinning sensor: the drawing shows a flat rectangular board module lying horizontally, with no cylinder, no drum, no dome and nothing rotating anywhere. A small square photonic chip sits at the center of the board, its surface etched with fine waveguide lines that run from an edge-coupled laser, split at a Y-junction into a transmit path leaving the chip edge and a local-oscillator path curving back, and recombine at a coupler feeding a pair of small balanced photodetectors. Flat, planar, chip-scale.
prompts.4: A millimeter-wave radar board: a small square circuit board with a fingernail-sized radar chip at its center and an array of diamond-shaped patch antennas etched directly onto the board surface in neat rows above and below the chip. A connector at one edge. No lens and no window.
prompts.5: An ultrasonic ranger: two cylindrical transducer cans mounted side by side on a small board, one of them emitting a widening cone of concentric arc wavefronts toward a flat plate, the arcs returning to the other. Show the wide cone angle.
prompts.6: A machine-vision camera: a rectangular body with a C-mount lens barrel and focus ring on the front, cut away along its axis to show the lens elements and a small CMOS sensor die sitting at the image plane on a board. Ribbon connector at the rear.
prompts.7: A stereo depth camera: a long slim horizontal bar module with a lens at each far end and a small pattern projector between them, mounted on a bracket. Faint straight sight lines run from both lenses and converge on a small cube in front, showing the triangulation baseline.
prompts.8: A structured-light depth camera: a module with a lens beside an illumination emitter, the emitter casting a regular grid of dots onto a simple curved object in front of it. The dot grid is visibly bent and stretched where it falls across the object's curvature, and evenly spaced elsewhere.
prompts.9: An event camera cut away at the focal plane to show its pixel grid: a uniform array of square pixels of which only a thin scattered line is active, tracing the leading edge of a moving object, while every other pixel is blank. The sparse active line is the focus.
prompts.10: A thermal camera: a compact rectangular body with a smooth dark germanium lens that shows no internal glass elements, cut away to reveal a microbolometer focal plane array mounted on a substrate inside a sealed vacuum package behind the lens.
prompts.11: A MEMS inertial sensor die at extreme magnification: a square silicon chip carrying a rectangular proof mass suspended on folded serpentine springs between rows of fine comb fingers, with a separate tuning-fork gyroscope structure etched alongside it. Bond pads around the die edge.
prompts.12: A fiber-optic gyroscope: a flat circular spool wound with many visible turns of optical fiber, both fiber ends running to a small coupler and light source block at the side. Beside it, a solid triangular ring-laser block with a mirror at each of its three corners and a bore drilled along each side.
prompts.13: A survey-grade GNSS antenna: a disc-shaped choke-ring antenna made of several concentric upright circular ridges around a central radiating element, mounted on a short threaded post, with a coaxial cable running to a small receiver box below.
prompts.14: An ultra-wideband positioning pair: a flat rectangular anchor module on a wall bracket with a wideband antenna trace visible on its board, and a much smaller tag module opposite it, with faint expanding arc wavefronts travelling between the two.
prompts.15: Cutaway of a rotary encoder: a finely graduated code disc mounted on a shaft, with an LED source on one side and a photodetector array on the other reading through the disc's slots, plus a bearing and a housing with a cable gland. Show the fine radial graduations on the disc.
prompts.16: Cutaway of a resolver: a laminated iron stator with heavy windings in its slots and a wound laminated rotor on a shaft inside it, coupled through a rotary transformer at one end. Rugged and simple, with no circuit board, no optics and no semiconductors anywhere.
prompts.17: A linear encoder: a long graduated scale strip fixed along a machine way, its fine graduation lines drawn along its length, with a compact read head riding just above it on a moving carriage and a cable trailing from the head.
prompts.18: A six-axis force-torque sensor: a thick disc cut open at the top face to show a machined spoke flexure inside, three slender beams joining a central hub to the outer ring, with small strain gauge patches bonded flat on the beam faces. A bolt circle around the rim.
prompts.19: A tactile skin: a thin flexible laminated sheet printed with a regular grid of square sensing pads, wrapping over a curved robot fingertip, with one corner of the sheet peeled back to expose the layered construction underneath. A flat ribbon tail leaves the sheet.
prompts.20: Cutaway of a vision-based tactile fingertip: a soft transparent elastomer pad at the top being indented by a small ridged object, a ring of small LEDs around the inside edge lighting the pad from shallow angles, and a small camera at the bottom of the chamber looking up at the deformed underside of the pad.
prompts.21: A motor drive board with a small current-shunt resistor and its sense traces picked out on the board, connected by three phase wires to a motor at the elbow of a robot arm link. The joint itself carries no sensor of any kind, and the empty joint is as important as the board.

partPrompts.1: A mechanical spinning LiDAR sitting upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a squat cylindrical unit whose upper drum carries one continuous dark horizontal window band running the whole way around it, standing on a plain base with a connector at the bottom. Exterior view only, not a cutaway. The unbroken band around the drum is the identifying feature, and the unit has real height, so it reads as a drum and not as a thin flat disc.
partPrompts.2: A millimeter-wave radar module lying flat on a surface, seen three-quarter: a thin rectangular circuit board whose upper face carries a neat array of identical diamond-shaped antenna patches etched flat onto the surface in two rows, with one small square chip package between the rows and a connector at one edge. Flat and plate-like. No lens, no window, no dome, no drum, and nothing protruding above the board except the low chip.
partPrompts.3: An industrial camera standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a compact rectangular body with a cylindrical lens barrel projecting well out from its front face, the barrel stepped and ringed with a knurled focus band, and a round glass front element swelling out of the rim as a shallow dome so the curve reads clearly in profile. Exterior view only, not a cutaway. The protruding barrel and its domed glass are what must read.
partPrompts.4: A tactical-grade inertial measurement unit alone on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a small milled metal block a little taller than it is wide, with a flat mounting foot carrying one bolt hole at each corner and a single round multi-pin connector on one side face. Sealed and blank all over: no lens, no window, no antenna patches, no dome and no opening of any kind anywhere on it. This is the sensor that looks at nothing, and the blank exterior is the point.
partPrompts.5: An encoder code disc lying at a slight angle on a flat surface: one thin flat round disc with a bold ring of evenly spaced radial slots cut through it near the rim, coarse enough to count, and a plain raised hub with a center bore in the middle. The outer edge of the disc is a smooth unbroken circle, not toothed. One thin disc on its own, not a drum, with no housing, no cable, no shaft and no electronics.
partPrompts.6: A tactile skin sheet lying alone on a flat surface: a thin limp flexible sheet printed with a bold regular grid of square sensing pads, one corner curling up off the surface so the sheet clearly reads as floppy rather than rigid, with a flat ribbon tail leaving one edge. Soft and sheet-like, with no housing, no disc, no circuit board and nothing rigid anywhere.
